dati_metodo: 46,976 portfolio company-round pairs, 15,786 US VC-backed companies, VentureXpert, 1975-2005; Weibull accelerated-failure-time model of the duration between adjacent financing rounds, with right-censoring and SEs clustered by company; Cox, exponential and log-normal give unaltered results

righe.estrazione: Li frames the staging decision as a choice between holding the current option to invest and investing now. In the empirical results, higher market uncertainty goes with longer durations to the next round, while competition, project-specific uncertainty and agency concerns go with shorter ones. This supports the tesi that round durations respond to uncertainty in the direction a real-options view predicts.
righe.citazione: The empirical results suggest that market uncertainty encourages venture capital firms to delay investing at each round of financing, whereas competition, project-specific uncertainty and agency concerns prompt venture capital firms to invest sooner.
righe.frase_paper: Li (2008) finds, in a sample of US VC-backed companies, that round durations lengthen with market uncertainty and shorten with competition and project-specific uncertainty, as a real-options view predicts.
righe.frase_slide: Higher market uncertainty goes with longer waits to the next round (Li, 2008)
righe.numero_chiave: 46,976 company-round pairs, 15,786 portfolio companies, US, 1975-2005 (sample size)
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Sample 1975-2005 from VentureXpert, not 2012-2019 PitchBook; the outcome is the duration between rounds, not exit; market uncertainty is measured as industry price volatility (GARCH), not our heat. The paper speaks of VC firms' decisions, our design is about startup-level associations.
righe.note: The tesi says only 'respond to uncertainty'; the txt is more specific (market uncertainty delays, project-specific uncertainty and competition accelerate). Direction is consistent with the tesi.

righe.estrazione: Li models the time between two adjacent rounds with a Weibull accelerated-failure-time model, ln T = Xb + e, whose coefficients are read as effects on log duration. The hazard function of the Weibull is stated, and a Cox model and other parametric models are mentioned as giving unaltered results. The framework is real options. So the study is a duration analysis, but the main model is an AFT specification rather than a hazard regression.
righe.citazione: To estimate the effects of the real options and agency factors on the funding duration, we consider an accelerated- failure-time (AFT) model:
righe.frase_paper: Li (2008) models the duration between financing rounds with a Weibull accelerated-failure-time model, with right-censoring, in a real-options framework.
righe.frase_slide: Round duration modelled with a Weibull duration model in a real-options frame (Li, 2008)
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Duration of spells between rounds is the dependent variable; we use the gap only as a regressor for exit in a logit.
righe.note: 'Hazard models' is imprecise: the main model is an AFT Weibull on log duration (it defines a hazard function; the Cox model is only a robustness check reported as unaltered).

righe.estrazione: Same point as the other methods row: Li studies the time between adjacent financing rounds with a Weibull accelerated-failure-time model on the log of duration, accounting for right-censoring. A semi-parametric Cox model and exponential or log-normal models give unaltered results, but they are not the main specification.
righe.citazione: The empirical analysis focuses on the funding duration, i.e., the time elapsed between two adjacent rounds of financing for a portfolio company.
righe.frase_paper: Li (2008) analyses the time elapsed between adjacent financing rounds with a Weibull duration model that accounts for right-censoring.
righe.frase_slide: Time between rounds analysed with a duration model (Li, 2008)
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Round duration is the outcome in Li; in our design the gap is an explanatory variable for exit.
righe.note: The tesi 'hazard models of round duration' is narrowed to the Weibull AFT specification; the tesi also adds '(a model of point 1)', not checkable in the txt.
